about: Proposed region definitions for detailed maps of Mexico: 32 states (entidades federativas), one region each. See docs/REGIONS-MX.md.

codes.proposal: ISO 3166-2:MX state codes, MX-AGU to MX-ZAC (three letters after MX-).
codes.why: The three-letter suffixes do not collide with any US state code in STATE_CODES (engine/address_search.py), which are two letters. A bare MX is not a US code.
codes.verified: The ISO 3166-2:MX codes were not checked against the ISO site in this change.

INEGI-Libre-Uso.name: Términos de Libre Uso de la Información del INEGI
INEGI-Libre-Uso.attribution: Fuente: INEGI, <product name>, e.g. "Fuente: INEGI, Marco Geoestadístico 2023". Notify end users of any analysis or transformation; do not suggest INEGI endorses the result.

CC-BY-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
CC-BY-4.0.attribution: Credit the publisher (Google Open Buildings: "Google Open Buildings"; Overture: see attribution page).

terrain.dataset: CEM 4.0 (Continuo de Elevaciones Mexicano, ~15 m, bare-earth DTM, COG)
terrain.notes: National bare-earth model at ~15 m, close to the 30 m the app uses today. CEM 4.0 derived from ALOS PALSAR (JAXA) with LiDAR gap-filling; coverage complete over continental Mexico, partial over islands. Download by state or by area.
Surface model: follows canopy and roofs.

water.dataset: INEGI Red Hidrográfica Nacional (rivers, lakes, streams; WMS/SHP)
water.verified: search only (product page not opened directly)
water.notes: National hydrographic network at 1:250,000. Download as shapefile from INEGI.

water.licence: not stated on the page (search only)
water.notes: ArcGIS REST service; layer 'Ríos Principales' (layer 3). Licence not confirmed.

dams.dataset: CONAGUA Catálogo de Presas (dam catalog, CSV, 210+ dams with coordinates)
dams.licence: not stated on the page (search only)
dams.verified: catalog page opened 2026-11-18; CSV not downloaded (redirect loop); dam count (~210) seen in search results; licence not confirmed
dams.notes: Fields: name, latitude, longitude, altitude, state, municipality, basin, hydrological region. ArcGIS REST also available at sigagis.conagua.gob.mx.

crops.dataset: INEGI Conjunto de datos vectoriales de uso del suelo y vegetación, escala 1:250,000, serie VII (2018)
crops.notes: National land-use and vegetation at 1:250,000, series I (1992) to VII (2018). Includes crop types specific to Mexico (agave, agostadero, temporal, etc.) that have no US class. The mapping to orchard/vineyard/berry + Mexican crops would need new kinds.

crops.dataset: ESA WorldCover 2021, 10 m (land cover, not crop types)
crops.notes: 10 m land cover, not crop types. Coarser than the INEGI vegetation data.

buildings.dataset: Google Open Buildings V3 (building footprints from satellite imagery)
buildings.notes: 1.8B building detections across Africa, Latin America, Caribbean, South Asia and SE Asia. Mexico is covered. CC BY 4.0 and ODbL; user may choose either. Confidence scores provided.
OSM has building footprints in urban areas; coverage is thinner in rural Mexico.

places.dataset: INEGI Marco Geoestadístico (AGEE, AGEM, localidades; names and codes)
places.notes: National framework of states (AGEE), municipalities (AGEM) and localities. Updated yearly; version 2025 available. Also includes 2,467 municipalities and 16 demarcaciones territoriales of Mexico City.

addresses.publisher: Overture Maps Foundation, from INEGI through OpenAddresses
addresses.verified: opened and rows counted 2026-11-18 (Overture address guide)
addresses.notes: Release 2026-11-18.0: 30,726,687 MX rows, the second-largest country after the US (126,202,222). Source: 'INEGI, Censos Económicos. Términos de Libre Uso. Distributed by OpenAddresses. Accessed: 2026-11-17.' Per-state counts not computed for this proposal; would need a DuckDB query by state.

not_open_nationwide: Postcode areas: Mexico has no open national postcode-area layer. SEPOMEX (the postal service) owns postcode data but does not publish areas as open data. INEGI's Marco Geoestadístico includes locality points, not postcode areas.

postal_code.format: Five digits (CP, código postal); the first two are the state (01-32), so leading zeros are common (01xxx Aguascalientes, 32xxx Zacatecas). Same shape as a US ZIP code.

addressing.order: Street type, street name, then number, then postcode and town: "Av. Reforma, 123, 06600 Ciudad de México". The type comes first (Avenida, Calle, Boulevard, Privada, Andador) and is often abbreviated (Av., C., Blvd., Priv., And.).
addressing.notes: normalize() and norm() keep only a-z and 0-9; Spanish accents (á, é, í, ó, ú, ñ) and Mexican street abbreviations would need folding on both sides, as noted for Spain. Mexican addresses sometimes use 'S/N' (sin número, 'no number'), like the Spanish 'S-N'. is_address_query() needs a number first, so "Av. Reforma 123, 06600" is not treated as an address today. tools/build_addresses.py keeps only country = 'US'; would need to accept country = 'MX'. Checked in this repository on 2026-11-18.
